info.title: Paladin Agent API
info.description: HTTP API for executing and managing resident Paladin agents. Agent routes are served under `/v1`; `/health`, `/ready`, and the docs are unversioned.

get.summary: `GET /agents` — list every registered agent as a safe [`AgentSummary`].
get.description:
Always returns `200 OK` with a JSON array (empty when no agents are registered).
Order is unspecified.

post.summary: `POST /agents` — register a new agent at runtime from an [`AgentSpec`].

get.description:
Returns `200 OK` with the agent's [`AgentSummary`], or `404 Not Found` with
`{ "error": ... }` if no agent is registered under `id`.

delete.description:
Returns `204 No Content` (empty body) on success, or `404 Not Found` with
`{ "error": ... }` if no agent is registered under `id`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Registry id of the agent to remove

post.summary: `POST /agents/{id}/execute` — look the agent up by id and run it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Registry id of the agent to run

403.description: Role not permitted for this agent

post.summary: `POST /agents/{id}/execute/stream` — run an agent, streaming its output over SSE.
post.description:
Returns a `text/event-stream` of `chunk` events ending with a `done` event. For an
agent with a streaming backend these are real incremental LLM tokens; for an agent
without one, the buffered result is framed as a single `chunk` + `done` (so the
endpoint always works). Execution is bounded by the resolved timeout: on expiry the
stream yields a terminal `error` event (streaming) or returns `504` (buffered
fallback). Maps unknown id → `404`, invalid `timeout_seconds` → `400`, and an
up-front execution failure → `502`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Registry id of the agent to run

200.description: Server-Sent Events stream: `chunk` events carry `{ "text": ... }`, a terminal `done` event carries the final result, and an `error` event (with the standard error envelope) is emitted on mid-stream failure or timeout.

403.description: Role not permitted for this agent

post.summary: `POST /agents/{id}/jobs` — enqueue an async run and return its job id immediately.
post.description:
Spawns a task that runs the agent (buffered) under the resolved timeout, recording
the outcome in the job store. Returns `202 Accepted` with `{ "job_id": ... }`. Maps
unknown id → `404` and invalid `timeout_seconds` → `400`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Registry id of the agent to run

403.description: Role not permitted for this agent

get.summary: `GET /agents/{id}/jobs/{job_id}` — poll an async job's status and result.
get.description:
Returns `200 OK` with the [`JobRecord`], or `404` if no
job is found under `job_id` (jobs are ephemeral and may have been evicted).

get.summary:
`GET /assistants` -- paginated list, merged with synthetic code-registry entries
(D-32). Authenticated, any role.
get.description:
Returns `200 OK` with [`AssistantListResponse`] on success, or `501 Not Implemented`
if no assistant admin backend is configured.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page's next_cursor

200.description: A page of assistants, merged with synthetic code-registry entries when expose_code_registry is on

400.description: Invalid assistant id, unknown kind, or a definition that fails validation -- violations in `details`

409.description: already_exists, or code_registered_immutable if the id is code-registered

get.summary:
`GET /assistants/{id}` -- one assistant, falling back to a synthetic code-registry
entry (D-32) when not found in the stored repository. Authenticated, any role.

`GET /assistants/{id}/versions` -- paginated version history, ascending by `version`
(PLAT-FR-10 changelog). Authenticated, any role.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page's next_cursor

200.description: A page of versions, ascending by version

400.description: Invalid assistant id, or limit exceeds 100
Invalid assistant id or a definition that fails validation -- violations in `details`

get.summary:
`GET /assistants/{id}/versions/{version}` -- one version, falling back to a synthetic
version-1 response (D-32) for a code-registered id when `version == 1`. Authenticated,
any role.

404.description: version 0, version above latest, or unknown assistant

409.description: Thread busy -- the remedy is POST /threads/{id}/resume

get.summary:
`GET /runs/{run_id}/stream` -- Server-Sent Events stream of a run's
progress (PLAT-FR-07, D-24..D-27).

200.description: Server-Sent Events stream of the seven frozen wire events (D-25): `superstep` `{ superstep }`, `node_started` `{ superstep, node_id }`, `node_finished` `{ superstep, node_id, outcome }`, `state_delta` `{ superstep, fields, bytes }` (changed field NAMES and a byte-size count only -- never a value), `parley` `{ waypoint_id, parleys }`, `done` `{ status, waypoint_id }` and `error` `{ status, message, waypoint_id }`. Every event also carries `seq`, `at`, `mode` (`live` or `degraded`) and `dropped`. The degraded path (the run executes on another instance, or is already terminal) gives no ordering guarantee relative to the live path and may coalesce supersteps; `done`/`error` are always eventually delivered on both paths. A 15s heartbeat comment line defeats idle proxy timeouts on both paths.

501.description: No run event stream backend configured

get.description:
Returns `200 OK` with [`ScheduleListResponse`] on success, or `501 Not Implemented` if no
schedule admin backend is configured.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page's next_cursor

400.description: Invalid cron, timezone, assistant reference, webhook URL, or thread strategy -- violations in `details`

get.summary:
`GET /schedules/{id}` -- one schedule, including `last_tick`/`next_tick`/`skipped_ticks`
(D-39). Authenticated, any role.

patch.summary:
`PATCH /schedules/{id}` -- partial update (admin). A `cron`/`timezone` change
recomputes `next_tick`; `enabled: false` leaves `next_tick` in place (D-39); a `webhook`
change re-runs the write-time SSRF guard (D-42).

400.description: Invalid schedule id, cron, timezone, webhook URL, or thread strategy -- violations in `details`

get.description:
Authenticated, any role (D-24) -- see [`get_thread_state`]'s docs on why
reads are not admin-gated the way [`resume_thread`] is.

`limit` (at most [`MAX_HISTORY_LIMIT`]) and an opaque `cursor` whose
content is the last returned item's `waypoint_id` (D-27). Returns
`400 Bad Request` for `limit > 100` or an unparseable `cursor`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page's next_cursor

400.description: limit exceeds 100, or cursor is not a valid waypoint id

post.description:
Requires an admin principal ([`require_admin`]) -- see the module-level
"Authorization" docs: this narrows D-24's "any role" default for the one
*mutating* thread route (CR-01, 24-REVIEW.md), pending PLAT-06's real
per-thread ownership scoping.

Validates synchronously through [`ParleyPort::resume_with`] and returns
`202 Accepted` immediately; the run itself continues on a background task
(D-25) -- a client polls `GET .../state` to observe the outcome. Maps
[`ParleyError`] per [`map_parley_error`].

202.description: Resume accepted; poll GET /threads/{id}/state for the outcome

400.description: One of unknown_parley_id / parley_already_answered / response_shape_invalid / parley_expired; the offending parley_id is in `details`

409.description: Same HTTP status, two distinct envelope codes: `thread_not_awaiting_input` (the thread is not suspended) or `graph_not_registered` (the thread's graph fingerprint has no registered WarGraph in this process)

get.summary:
`GET /threads/{id}/state` -- the thread's latest status, plus outstanding
parleys/responses when suspended.

AgentSpec.description:
Declarative description of an agent to provision at runtime.

Sent in the body of `POST /agents`. Because `paladin-web` cannot itself build a
[`Paladin`] (that needs an `LlmPort` and the builder, which live behind the
facade), an [`AgentProvisioner`] turns this spec into a concrete
`(Paladin, executor)` pair.

Only the fields needed to identify and shape an agent are included here; the
provisioner is free to apply defaults for everything else. More fields can be
added without breaking existing callers (all optional fields use `#[serde(default)]`).

allowed_roles.description: Roles permitted to invoke this agent (`"admin"`/`"user"`); empty ⇒ any caller.

id.description: Registry id (the path segment in `/agents/{id}/…`). Client-supplied and unique.

stop_words.description: Optional stop words that terminate execution.

system_prompt.description: System prompt defining the agent's behavior.

temperature.description: Optional response randomness (`0.0`–`1.0`); the provisioner applies a default when absent.

timeout_seconds.description: Optional per-agent execution timeout (seconds); `None` uses the server default.

AgentSummary.description:
Safe, public-facing summary of an agent for the discovery endpoints.

Deliberately omits anything sensitive. Note that secrets (API keys, provider
credentials) never live on the [`Paladin`] entity in the first place — they are
supplied to executors at composition time — so none can leak here. The raw system
prompt is reduced to a short `description` preview rather than returned verbatim
(see PRD Open Question 1 on whether to omit it entirely).

description.description: Short, single-line preview derived from the system prompt.

ApiErrorBody.description:
OpenAPI schema for the error envelope returned by every failing handler.

Mirrors [`ApiError::to_body`] (`{ "error": { "code", "message", "details" } }`); it exists
purely so the generated spec can describe error responses. The runtime body is built by
`ApiError`, not this type.

items.description: The page of assistants, in the documented order.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, `None` on the last page.

AssistantResponse.description: Response body for `GET /assistants/{id}` and one item of `GET /assistants`.

created_at.description: When this assistant was first created.

deleted_at.description: When this assistant was soft-deleted, if it has been.

latest.description: The most recently published version number.

items.description: The page of versions, ascending by `version`.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, `None` on the last page.

AssistantVersionResponse.description: Response body for `GET/POST` on a single version.

assistant_id.description: The assistant this version belongs to.

created_by.description: Who published this version, if known.

assistant_id.description: The assistant this schedule submits runs against.

enabled.description: Whether this schedule starts out active.

input.description: The input every tick's submitted run receives.

thread_strategy.description:
`"new_thread_per_tick"` or `{ "fixed_thread": "<thread id>" }` (mirrors
`RunSchedule::thread_strategy`'s own wire shape); omitted for the default
(`new_thread_per_tick`).

timezone.description: The IANA timezone the cron expression is evaluated in, or omitted for `"UTC"`.

version.description: A specific version, or omitted to resolve `latest` at each tick.

oneOf.description: An optional webhook delivery target, validated by the write-time SSRF guard (D-42).

DefinitionDto.description: The wire shape of an assistant definition: `{ kind: "agent" | "workflow", body }`.

ExecuteRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /agents/{id}/execute`.

Only `input` is required today; later epics may add optional fields (streaming
flags, per-call overrides) without breaking this contract.

input.description: The task / prompt to run the agent against.

timeout_seconds.description: Optional per-request timeout (seconds), clamped to the server max. `0` is rejected.

ExecuteResponse.description:
Response body for a successful agent execution.

Carries the agent output plus the safe execution metadata from
[`PaladinResult`]. The `stop_reason` is rendered as a stable lowercase label
(`"completed"`, `"max_loops"`, `"stop_word"`, `"timeout"`) rather than the raw
serde enum shape, so the wire contract is stable.

stop_reason.description: Why execution stopped, as a stable label.

HistoryResponse.description:
Response body for `GET /threads/{id}/history`.

`next_cursor` is `None` on the last page; otherwise it is the last
returned item's `waypoint_id`, opaque to clients (D-27) -- its internal
structure may change (PLAT-06) without this being a breaking change.

items.description: The page of waypoint summaries, newest-first.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or `None` on the last page.

JobRecord.description:
A stored job: its status plus, when finished, a result or error.

`result` is the serialized success payload (an `ExecuteResponse` as JSON), kept as a
[`Value`] so the store stays decoupled from the controller's wire types.

result.description: Success payload (an `ExecuteResponse` as JSON), present once `status == Completed`.

JobStatus.description: Lifecycle status of an async job.

ParleyRequestDto.description:
Wire projection of a [`ParleyRequest`] (a `paladin-core` type) into a
`utoipa::ToSchema` type this crate owns (ADR-0038).

expires_at.description: When this parley expires, if ever.

node_id.description: The node that raised this parley.

prompt.description: Free-form prompt describing what input is being awaited.

defaulted.description:
Whether this response was substituted by an `on_expire` default
rather than submitted by a caller.

responded_by.description: Who submitted this response, if known.

ParleyResponseInput.description:
One submitted answer inside a [`ResumeRequest`].

`kind`/`prompt` are intentionally absent: `WarEngine::resume_with`
stamps both onto the persisted response from the matching request's own
fields, regardless of what a caller supplies (D-07) -- so this DTO never
asks a client to know or repeat them.

responded_by.description: Who is submitting this response, if the caller wants it recorded.

value.description: The submitted value, validated per the parley's own `kind`.

PatchScheduleRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH /schedules/{id}` -- every field optional; only fields present
change (D-39's "`enabled: false` leaves `next_tick` in place" applies at the port layer).

cron.description: A new cron expression, if changing it.

enabled.description: A new enabled flag, if changing it.

input.description: A new input, if changing it.

on_missed.description: A new missed-tick policy (`"skip"` or `"run_once"`), if changing it.

thread_strategy.description:
A new thread strategy, if changing it -- same wire shape as
[`CreateScheduleRequest::thread_strategy`].

timezone.description: A new timezone, if changing it.

oneOf.description: A new webhook target, if changing it -- re-validated by the write-time SSRF guard.

ResumeAcceptedResponse.description:
Response body for a successful `POST /threads/{id}/resume` (`202 Accepted`).

`#[non_exhaustive]` (D-21, PLAT-03): `run_id` was added after this type
shipped in Phase 24, mirroring
[`ResumeAccepted`](paladin_ports::input::parley_port::ResumeAccepted)'s
own field of the same name and meaning one level down the stack.
Construction stays possible only through [`Self::new`] (X-10.3), so the
next field stays free without a semver-major bump.

run_id.description:
The run this resume re-enqueued, if the durable run-server path
handled it (`None` for Phase 24's in-process-spawn fallback, X-03).

state_url.description: The URL a client polls (`GET .../state`) to observe the outcome.

thread_id.description: The thread whose resume was accepted.

responses.description: Every response to submit in this call.

error.description: The engine's error, if this run is `Failed`.

finished_at.description: When this run reached a terminal status, if it has.

started_at.description: When this run entered `Running`, if it has.

status.description:
Stable, lowercase status label (the same strings `RunStatus::as_str`
returns).

thread_id.description: The thread this run executes against.

items.description: The page of schedules, in the documented order.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, `None` on the last page.

ScheduleResponse.description:
Response body for `GET /schedules/{id}` and one item of `GET /schedules` -- every
[`RunSchedule`] field, including `last_tick`/`next_tick`/`skipped_ticks` so "why did
nothing run" is answerable without a log dive (D-39).

assistant_id.description: The assistant this schedule submits runs against.

enabled.description: Whether this schedule is currently active.

input.description: The input every tick's submitted run receives.

last_tick.description: The last tick this schedule fired (or was claimed) at, if any.

next_tick.description: The next tick this schedule is due at, if scheduled.

skipped_ticks.description: How many ticks have been skipped (D-39's counted metric).

timezone.description: The IANA timezone the cron expression is evaluated in.

updated_at.description: When this schedule was last updated.

version.description: A specific version, or `null` to resolve `latest` at each tick.

oneOf.description: The webhook delivery target, if any -- `secret` redacted to `"***"` (T-27-14-03).

SubmitRunRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /runs`.

`input` defaults to an empty object: submit-time validation checks only
the assistant reference and this body's shape, never `input`'s own
schema -- a schema violation surfaces later as a `Failed` run.

thread_id.description: An existing thread to run against, or omitted to start a fresh one.

version.description: A specific version, or omitted to resolve `latest` at submit time.

SubmitRunResponse.description: Response body for a successful `POST /runs` (`202 Accepted`).

state_url.description: The URL a client polls (`GET /runs/{run_id}`) to observe status.

thread_id.description: The thread the run executes against.

ThreadStateResponse.description:
Response body for `GET /threads/{id}/state`.

`parleys`/`responses` are always present, empty unless `status` is
`"awaiting_input"` (Test 2: a running/completed thread carries the
summary fields with no outstanding parleys, not an omitted key).

fork_of.description:
The ROOT `WaypointId` of the branch this Waypoint belongs to;
`None` for a mainline Waypoint (HITL-03, D-14).

parleys.description:
Every parley raised in the suspending superstep, when `status` is
`"awaiting_input"`; empty otherwise.

responses.description:
The accepted subset of responses so far, when `status` is
`"awaiting_input"`; empty otherwise.

superstep.description: The superstep index of the returned Waypoint.

fork_of.description:
The ROOT `WaypointId` of the branch this waypoint belongs to;
`None` for a mainline waypoint.

parent_waypoint_id.description: The waypoint this one was checkpointed from.

superstep.description: The superstep index that produced this waypoint.

WebhookRequestDto.description: Wire shape of a webhook delivery target on write (`POST`/`PATCH`).

events.description:
The lifecycle events this webhook subscribes to (`"awaiting_input"`, `"completed"`,
`"failed"`, `"halted"`, `"cancelled"`).

secret.description: The HMAC signing secret, if any.

url.description:
The delivery URL -- validated by the write-time SSRF guard (D-42) before the
schedule is ever persisted.

WebhookResponseDto.description:
Wire shape of a webhook delivery target on read -- the SAME shape as
[`WebhookRequestDto`], except `secret` is redacted (T-27-14-03).

events.description: The lifecycle events this webhook subscribes to.

secret.description:
`"***"` when a secret is set on the stored schedule, `null` otherwise -- the raw
secret is never echoed back.
